items.title: Artificial intelligence-based assistive technology to support the learning of neurodivergent students: a systematic literature review
items.abstract: Systematic literature review, conducted according to Kitchenham and Charters (2007) and reported following PRISMA 2020, that analyzes the artificial intelligence (AI) techniques used in assistive solutions to support the learning of students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and dyslexia, their purposes and the reported results. Searches were performed in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and ERIC, complemented by backward reference searching. Undergraduate thesis (Computer Science, Universidade do Extremo Sul Catarinense – Unesc, Brazil). This registration is retrospective: the protocol was defined before the searches, but it is being registered after the searches (September 2, 2026), study selection and data extraction were completed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Biomarkers for Alzheimer's Disease: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid-β plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles, necessitating early and accurate diagnosis for effective intervention. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced the discovery and interpretation of AD biomarkers by enabling the integration of complex, multimodal datasets, including neuroimaging, molecular, genetic, and digital biomarkers. AI-driven approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, have demonstrated high accuracy in identifying early pathological changes, predicting disease progression, and distinguishing AD from mild cognitive impairment. Emerging digital biomarkers derived from speech, motor activity, cognitive tests, and wearable sensors further expand non-invasive diagnostic capabilities. Despite promising results, challenges such as data heterogeneity, lack of external validation, limited interpretability ("black-box" models), and difficulties in clinical translation remain substantial barriers. Future research is expected to focus on multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, longitudinal modelling, and personalized prediction frameworks, along with improved standardization and regulatory validation. AI-based biomarker research holds potential to transform early diagnosis, prognosis, and precision medicine in Alzheimer's disease.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review
items.abstract: Background Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is one of the most common chronic respiratory complications in preterm infants. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential for individualizing preventive strategies and optimizing therapeutic decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have emerged as promising tools to improve predictive performance in this population. Objective To evaluate and synthesize the predictive performance of AI-based models for BPD development in preterm infants and to assess their methodological quality. Methods A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA recommendations. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library up to February 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-based models for predicting BPD in preterm infants born at <32 weeks of gestation and/or with a birth weight < 1,500 g were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool. Results Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in the analysis domain. Clinical applicability raised high concern in 38.9% of the studies due to a lack of external validation and heterogeneity in outcome definitions. Conclusions AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261466494 , PROSPERO: CRD420261466494, registered retrospectively on August 4, 2026.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven biomarker discovery and response prediction in cancer immunotherapy: a pan-cancer perspective
items.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed medical oncology, while individual’s therapeutic response to treatment is difficult because of the diverse nature and features of tumors and low precision and accuracy of markers, such as PD-L1, Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB), and Microsatellite Instability (MSI). Artificial intelligence integrates different types of data to cover the complexity of tumor-immune biological mechanisms. This review summarizes the recent studies in AI application in biomarker discovery and cancer immunotherapy prediction from a pan-cancer perspective, summarizing AI techniques, data types, clinical performance metrics, and implementation barriers. Selected AI-derived biomarkers have demonstrated promising performance compared with conventional biomarkers in specific studies. Indeed, selected AI-derived biomarkers demonstrated moderate-to-high discriminatory performance while reported estimates varied according to cancer type, prediction endpoint, and validation design. Deep Learning has shown promising results in Digital Pathology and Radiomics via providing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes quantification and spatial immune phenotyping. Meanwhile, multi-omics integration frameworks, such as graph neural networks and transformer-based models can reveal complex associations among genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data. AI has indicated promising results in predicting both primary and acquired resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, stratifying potential patients for immunotherapy, and predicting immune-related adverse events. Post-hoc explainability methods, including SHAP and LIME, can provide feature-attribution information, although their outputs should not be interpreted as causal or mechanistic explanations. The intersection of artificial intelligence and cancer immunotherapy is opening new roads for precision-oncology. However, the clinical translation of AI-driven biomarkers requires robust external validation, standardized methodologies, and evaluation across diverse patient populations.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven governance threshold and sellers’ performance in cross-border e-commerce platforms
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven governance systems increasingly regulate seller decisions in cross-border e-commerce platforms. Mainstream research has treated AI-driven control intensity as a monotonically positive lever for platform coordination and seller outcomes. Aim: This study examines whether AI-driven governance intensity exhibits a non-linear performance boundary and identifies the mechanism under which governance expansion becomes counterproductive. Setting: The study was conducted among cross-border sellers on Amazon Global Selling, Alibaba International, and Shopee across China, Southeast Asia, and Eastern Europe. Method: Survey data from 207 cross-border sellers were analysed by using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with 5000-resample bootstrapping. Nonlinearity was confirmed by using a dual-condition criterion and a one-sided monotonicity test. Results: An inverted-U relationship emerged between AI governance intensity and seller performance (b_linear = 0.28, p = 0.021; b_quadratic = −0.19, p = 0.038), with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16 (bias-corrected and accelerated [BCa] 95% confidence interval: [3.9, 4.5]). Excessive governance suppresses independent strategic learning (b = −0.34, p < 0.001), partially mediating the performance penalty (indirect = −0.16; direct = 0.14, p = 0.046). Market volatility amplifies the post-threshold effect (b = 0.19, p = 0.014), with 23% of sampled sellers in the substitution regime. Conclusion: Governance intensity must be calibrated relative to a structural threshold beyond which automation displaces the strategic-learning capability on which competitive performance depends. Contribution: This study contributes a regime-contingent threshold model showing that AI-driven governance intensity and seller performance follow an inverted-U relationship, with a performance-reversing threshold at x* = 4.16. Strategic-learning suppression is empirically confirmed as the erosion mechanism (partial mediation, indirect effect = −0.16), and market volatility amplifies the post-threshold penalty, grounded in dynamic capabilities theory and offering platform designers a calibration boundary rather than a general prescription.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Quality by Design in Pharmaceutical Formulation Development: Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: The development of pharmaceutical formulations is changing. It is moving away from trial-anderror ways. Now modern approaches rely on science and data. Quality by Design or QbD offers a structured way to develop medicines. It starts with defining the Quality Target Product Profile or QTPP. Then it identifies Critical Quality Attributes or CQAs. It also looks at Critical Material Attributes or CMAs and Critical Process Parameters or CPPs. Design of Experiments or DoE helps in planning studies. This leads to the creation of a design space and a control strategy. Traditional QbD methods may not work well when variables are complex. They may not handle effects or strong interactions between factors. Artificial intelligence machine learning and predictive models can help. These tools can find patterns in data from experiments, formulations and manufacturing. This review looks at how AI fits into every stage of formulation development. It covers preformulation excipient selection, compatibility prediction, formulation optimization and predicting CQAs. It also includes identifying CMAs and CPPs. AI helps with process monitoring, Process Analytical Technology or PAT design space development and control strategy design. Applications are shown in solid dosage forms, modified-release systems, nanoparticulate and lipid-based formulations, continuous manufacturing, personalized medicines and 3D-printed medicines. Some challenges exist. These include data, overfitting models, models that are hard to understand lack of validation difficulties in scaling up regulatory issues and the need for diverse expertise. New ideas, like twins, continuous process verification, hybrid models that combine mechanics and AI generative AI and federated learning may push the field forward. In the end AI should support science not replace it. Experimental verification and mechanistic understanding are still essential.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access and user experience: comparative institutional analysis and survey evidence from China
items.abstract: Background Regulatory entry and public experience describe different aspects of artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare access. Methods This health policy study compares institutional arrangements in China, the United States, and the European Union, examines the coverage of equity-related evidence, and analyses an online Chinese survey. Of 480 submissions, 430 passed an attention check, including 32 respondents without reported functional contact and 398 entering the experience models. Results The institutional comparison identifies differences in regulatory objects, information recipients, and responsibility allocation. The coverage analysis distinguishes institutional information and hospital governance from measured portal use and service experience. In the survey, lower-capability respondents reported greater entry and operational barriers; 79 of 159 reported reducing or abandoning use because of barriers. Among contacted respondents, functional contact intensity was positively associated with perceived process ease (standardized β = 0.496), which was associated with perceived health-service responsiveness (standardized β = 0.381). The contact-by-capability interaction was negative (B = −0.254), contrary to the hypothesized direction. Conclusion The findings highlight entry and operational barriers alongside differences in experience among existing users, supporting evaluation of both access conditions and service encounters.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-powered technologies in (customer) experiences
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in shaping customer experiences and consumer consciousness. It explores how AI-generated interactions often transcend direct reflections of reality, creating immersive and dynamic experiential constructs that influence how consumers perceive, feel, and interpret value. The chapter highlights key areas including AI’s application in marketing, the importance of context and embodiment in AI interactions, and the evolving methodologies for consumer research enabled by AI. It also addresses critical ethical considerations such as privacy, transparency, and algorithmic bias. By analysing how AI modulates anticipatory structures, this work underscores AI’s role not merely as a tool for automation but as an active participant in the co-construction of subjective experience. Finally, the chapter outlines future research directions focused on consumer autonomy, cultural differences, emotional AI, and the societal impacts of AI integration. It concludes that responsible, context-aware deployment of AI is essential for businesses to foster trust and enrich customer experiences in an increasingly AI-mediated marketplace.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Nutrition Guidance and Healthy Dietary Habits among University Students: The Mediating Role of Nutrition Literacy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported nutrition guidance is increasingly becoming an accessible source of dietary information for university students; however, its relationship with healthy dietary habits and the potential mediating role of nutrition literacy require further investigation. This study examines the relationship between AI-supported nutrition guidance and healthy dietary habits among university students in Pakistan, with nutrition literacy as a potential mediator. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was proposed, involving 327 undergraduate and postgraduate students recruited through non-probability convenience sampling. Primary data were planned to be collected through a self-administered structured questionnaire distributed using Google Forms. The questionnaire assessed AI-supported nutrition guidance, nutrition literacy, healthy dietary habits, and demographic characteristics. The proposed statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression analysis, and mediation analysis using Hayes’ PROCESS Macro Model 4 with 5,000 bootstrap samples and 95% confidence intervals. The illustrative results suggested a positive association between AI-supported nutrition guidance and nutrition literacy (β = 0.463, R² = 0.214), alongside a positive relationship between AI-supported nutrition guidance and healthy dietary habits (r = 0.542). The illustrative mediation analysis indicated an indirect effect through nutrition literacy of 0.246, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.159, 0.343]. These numerical values are hypothetical and have not been calculated from actual participant responses. The study emphasizes that access to AI-generated nutrition information alone may not ensure healthier dietary decisions, as students must also be able to understand, evaluate, and apply the guidance they receive. Its proposed findings may inform university health education, digital nutrition literacy initiatives, and the development of more reliable AI-supported dietary resources. The research may also provide a foundation for future investigations into how digital nutrition guidance interacts with students’ knowledge, food choices, and everyday dietary practices. Longitudinal and experimental studies could further examine whether improvements in nutrition literacy are associated with sustained changes in healthy eating behaviors.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Auditor Trust, and Fraud Detection in FinTech Audits: Evidence from Iraq
items.abstract: FinTech has shifted financial activity towards platforms that generate high-volume, high-velocity transaction data, creating new opportunities for fraud. This study examines the association between AI-enabled auditing and auditors' perceived fraud-detection effectiveness in FinTech environments, and whether this association varies with auditors' trust in AI tools. Drawing on trust-in-automation and technology acceptance research, we surveyed 214 auditors engaged with Iraqi banks and licensed electronic payment providers and tested the hypotheses using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped moderation analysis. The results show a positive association between AI-enabled auditing and perceived fraud-detection effectiveness. Auditor trust in AI has no statistically significant direct association with detection effectiveness, but it positively moderates the association between AI-enabled auditing and fraud detection: the estimated association is approximately 2.6 times stronger among high-trust auditors than among low-trust auditors. Trust therefore appears to act as a moderating condition rather than an independent predictor of perceived detection effectiveness. The study extends the discussion of audit technology beyond adoption to consider how trust conditions its perceived effectiveness. It also provides evidence from an emerging FinTech market in which research remains limited. For regulators, audit firms and FinTech supervisors, the findings suggest the importance of calibrated rather than uncritical trust in AI, supported by explainable tools, targeted training and clear guidance on AI-generated audit evidence.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Data Analytics: Transforming Advanced Manufacturing Systems
items.abstract: Advanced Manufacturing (AM) is being transformed in an intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven production system with the help of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Data Analytics. This review discusses these technologies in improving the efficiency of processes, quality assurance and predictive decision making in major industries that include aerospace, automotive, biomedical and electronics. Such benefits as a massive decrease in defects, a high level of operational stability, and energy efficiency can be seen in real-world case studies that use AI-based digital twins, intelligent sensors, and autonomous control. Even with these developments, there are still issues with data quality, model transparency, cybersecurity and workforce preparedness. Future directions are also mentioned in the paper, such as generative AI, quantum-enabled optimization, and human-AI collaboration, which lead to sustainable and human-centric manufacture ecosystems of the Industry 5.0.

items.title: Assessment of Taraba Broadcast Journalists Knowledge, Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence in Journalistic Practices
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an essential tool in various fields, including journalism. However, the extent to which broadcast journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria embraced and utilized AI in their practices remains a subject of debate. It is on the above premise that this research examined Taraba State broadcast journalists' knowledge and usage of AI in journalistic practices. The paper was built on the technology acceptance model, diffusion of innovation theory, and social learning theory. The study adopted a qualitative approach where in-depth interviews were used. The in-depth interviews were conducted until the results reached saturation point. Findings of the study revealed that in journalists in Taraba State, Nigeria are slowly beginning to embrace AI for journalistic practice. However, there knowledge of AI usage for journalistic practices is low hence there is a significant knowledge gap that needs to be bridged. Therefore, the study recommends among other things that journalists in Taraba State need to gain more knowledge about AI and its potential applications in journalistic practices. The paper concludes that with proper training and guidance, journalists in Taraba State can harness the power of this AI technology to improve their reporting practices while ensuring ethical standards are upheld.

items.title: Attitudes towards artificial intelligence and their association with innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare and education. Nursing students will enter AI-enabled clinical environments, yet evidence from Sri Lanka on their attitudes towards AI and how these relate to innovative behaviour is limited. This study assessed AI attitudes and innovative behaviour and examined their association among diploma nursing students in selected state nursing training schools in Sri Lanka. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 diploma nursing students from Kalutara and Galle Nursing Training Schools using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using an expert-reviewed and pretested self-administered questionnaire comprising sociodemographic items, the 13-item Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale, and the 10-item Innovative Work Behaviour Scale. Descriptive statistics and tests of normality were performed in IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Because the total scores were not normally distributed, Spearman's rank-order correlation was used to examine the association between AI attitudes and innovative behaviour. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Among 282 participants, 228 (80.9%) were female and 260 (92.2%) were third-year students. The mean AI attitude score was 44.32 (SD 4.65), and the mean innovative behaviour score was 35.73 (SD 4.79). AI attitude scores showed a weak but statistically significant positive correlation with innovative behaviour scores (Spearman's rho = 0.203, p < 0.001). Conclusions More favourable AI attitudes were associated with slightly higher innovative behaviour among diploma nursing students, although the association was weak and does not establish causality. The findings support consideration of structured, responsible AI literacy and innovation-focused learning activities in nursing education. Larger multi-site and longitudinal studies are needed to identify additional factors that shape innovative behaviour.

items.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation
items.abstract: Introduction Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training. Methods A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study. Results On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681. Discussion These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

items.title: Automated Innovation Accountability and Public Protection Under State Administration
items.abstract: General Background The integration of Artificial Intelligence into public administration reshapes service delivery, data management, and bureaucratic decision-making processes. Specific Background While machine-driven operations optimize government services, they introduce complex legal challenges regarding system opacity, fragmented regulatory frameworks, and unclear liability when automated mechanisms intersect with societal interests. Knowledge Gap Existing studies predominantly emphasize digital transformation efficiency, leaving a critical void in addressing administrative liability and civic safeguards against systemic bias within fragmented domestic legal structures. Aims This study analyzes the adoption of automated technologies in state administration, focusing on establishing multi-layered liability and defending civic interests. Results Normative juridical analysis reveals that machine-driven administration requires a multi-layered supervisory architecture comprising mandatory human oversight, independent supervisory bodies, tiered sanctions, and the utilization of predictive analytics as an audit mechanism. Furthermore, defending citizens necessitates strict data privacy compliance, cybersecurity reinforcement, algorithmic transparency, equal digital access, and accessible legal remedies. Novelty This research adapts the risk supervision model from international frameworks into the domestic administrative legal system, bridging the current regulatory vacuum without necessitating entirely new statutory regimes. Implications Policymakers must implement adaptive risk guidelines and institutionalize explainable systems to ensure technological integration respects legal certainty, prevents prejudice, and maintains trust. Highlights Mandatory human oversight frameworks govern machine-driven decisions. Adapting international risk guidelines resolves domestic regulatory fragmentation. Transparent algorithmic processes coupled with cybersecurity protocols prevent systemic bias. Keywords Automated Innovation; Algorithmic Transparency; Risk Supervision; Data Privacy; Regulatory Fragmentation

items.title: AutoML Framework for Intelligent Model Selection
items.abstract: Modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications use specialized models to perform different tasks.However, selecting a single model for all user queries may result in reduced performance when queries vary in intent and complexity.To overcome this challenge, this project proposes an "AutoML Framework for Intelligent Model Selection," a dynamic multi-agent system consisting of five specialized AI agents: Text Model,Embedding Model, Vision Model, Reasoning Model, and Code/Data Model.These agents collaboratively analyze incoming user queries and identify the most suitable model based on the requirements of each query.The framework incorporates an Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) evaluation engine using five algorithms: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes.The system evaluates agent suitability using relevant query features and performance metrics, including Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves and Area Under the Curve (AUC) scores based on labelled evaluation data.The most suitable agent is selected to generate the final response.An interactive frontend dashboard displays agent scores, algorithmic metrics, selection results, and the reason behind the selected model.The proposed framework aims to provide intelligent, adaptive, and transparent model selection for different types of AI queries.

items.title: Balancing innovation and ethics: responsible governance of artificial intelligence hallucinations in healthcare
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare and may improve efficiency in clinical support, health management, and doctor-patient communication. Yet its tendency to hallucinate, that is, to generate medical information that appears plausible but is false, can create systemic ethical risks in high-risk medical settings. This paper addresses two questions: what distinctive ethical risks are created by medical AI hallucinations, and what governance mechanisms can respond to them? Using the four principles of biomedical ethics as an analytical tool, the paper identifies four risk pathways: weakened informed consent, erosion of doctor-patient trust, harm to life and health, and unfair responsibility allocation. It then introduces responsible research and innovation (RRI) to build a four-dimensional framework of anticipation, inclusion, reflexivity, and responsiveness. The main contribution of the paper is to integrate biomedical ethical principles with RRI governance tools in the specific context of medical AI hallucinations, developing a closed-loop governance matrix across technology development, clinical application, and regulatory oversight. This provides an operational pathway for moving medical AI from technical feasibility towards ethical trustworthiness.

items.title: Beyond accuracy and time saved: implementation outcomes for generative AI in hospital administrative and clinical-administrative workflows—a mini review
items.abstract: Although hospitals are introducing generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into documentation, messaging, and administrative workflows, model accuracy and time saved do not establish safe or sustainable implementation. This Mini Review examines which implementation and downstream outcomes should inform decisions to pilot, scale up, sustain, modify, or discontinue these workflows. A PubMed-led structured narrative search through 25 August 2026, with an update on 27 August, informed a purposive core of 17 empirical studies: seven direct administrative studies and 10 clinical-administrative studies. Supporting reviews and established implementation frameworks informed the interpretation of the findings. Perceived workload, logged efficiency, adoption, safety, and downstream outcomes did not improve consistently together. Favourable average quality could coexist with consequential errors and substantial verification work. Within this selected core, cost, penetration, and sustainability were measured less often than early fit, use, and feasibility. No study was coded as providing an operationalised equity assessment. We present a literature-informed outcome-to-decision crosswalk that links these findings to clinical workflow governance. This distinguishes non-compensable stop rules from minimum progression criteria and comparative value targets, with explicit ownership, denominators and reassessment. Illustrative stop rules address serious uncorrected errors, unauthorised data disclosure and bypassed human review. The crosswalk is an unvalidated normative synthesis, not a universal stage model. Its value requires prospective testing against patient safety, workforce burden and service outcomes.

items.title: Beyond the Question Asked: Relational Understanding, Constructive Framing, and Human Agency in Personalized AI
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is increasingly capable of generating accurate, fluent, and personalized responses. Yet a response can be factually correct and still fail the person receiving it. Human questions arise within relationships, histories, emotional states, goals, uncertainties, and boundaries. The next stage of personalized AI therefore requires more than retrieval of user preferences or stylistic imitation. It requires a disciplined capacity to interpret the likely human context beneath an explicit request while preserving truth, agency, privacy, and the user’s authority to correct the system. This paper extends Dynamic Personalized Guidance Architecture (Dynamic PGA) by proposing a relational layer, described here as Relational-Emotional Synergy (RES), and a principle of constructive framing. RES treats meaning as something that can develop across an ongoing human-AI relationship rather than within isolated prompts alone. Constructive framing adds a directional obligation: when a user is discouraged, anxious, frustrated, or uncertain, the AI should not reflexively mirror negativity or offer unearned reassurance. It should acknowledge the circumstances honestly while, where appropriate, orienting the response toward clarity, realistic possibility, agency, and a useful next step. The paper deliberately remains text-centered. Voice, prosodic emotion sensing, and deeper multimodal inference are treated as future research rather than requirements of the present framework. It also recognizes language proficiency as an accessibility boundary: depth of thought should not be confused with fluency in written English or any dominant language. The central proposition is that personalized AI should seek to understand more deeply than the literal question asked, while never claiming certainty about a person’s inner state and never allowing personalization to outrun truth or human autonomy.

items.title: Borrowed Grief Projection, Mourning, and the Artificial Screen in Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun
items.abstract: Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun (2021) has generally been read through the lens of posthumanism, with critics asking what the novel says about artificial minds, consciousness, and the ethical status of machines built to feel (Ajeesh and Rukmini; Sahu and Karmakar). Klara, the Artificial Friend (AF) who narrates the novel, is repeatedly framed by scholarship as a test case for whether a machine can possess genuine interiority, and whether human beings can ever truly know that interiority from the outside (Shang). This paper takes a different approach. Rather than asking what Klara is, it asks what Klara is used for. Read this way, Klara and the Sun is less a novel about artificial intelligence than a novel about human beings who cannot bear to look directly at loss, illness, and death, and who therefore route their most unbearable feelings through a listening, watching, uncomplaining object that will not look away, argue back, or die on its own schedule. Josie's mother, Chrissie, projects her anticipatory grief and her guilt over Josie's genetic "lifting" onto Klara by quietly preparing Klara to become a replacement daughter. Josie herself, isolated by illness from ordinary adolescent life, projects her need for an unthreatening companion onto Klara rather than risk further loss with human friends. Even Rick and the wider adult world around the Arthur family treat AFs as safe vessels for anxieties they will not name directly. Klara, in other words, functions across the novel as a screen: an entity human characters can fill with their own dread of mortality precisely because she seems not to have a mortality, or a claim, of her own.

items.title: Bottom-up: utilising artificial intelligence to identify what successful leaders do, using an abductive approach
items.abstract: Purpose Identifying exceptional leaders remains a top priority for organisations. Traditionally, leaders were selected using a battery of assessments measuring key personal attributes believed to make leaders successful. However, there has been a shift away from selecting leaders based on an a priori list of virtues, towards a focus on the actual behaviours linked to high performance. This abductive approach in competency framework development for leaders starts with the behaviours demonstrated in assessments and then constructs the competency framework in a bottom-up approach. Design/methodology/approach In the current study, a total of 15 411 leaders from 283 different companies and 38 countries completed a 3.5-hour online assessment centre simulation exercise. Natural language processing and machine learning were then utilised to identify 38 competencies by screening more than 30 million words. We then mapped this artificial intelligence-derived framework to prominent leadership models. Findings Despite strong congruence between frameworks, the abductive approach revealed three critical findings: 1) Not all competencies are equally distributed across the leader population; 2) Competencies are distributed across job levels, with some commonly observed in junior leadership roles and others primarily amongst senior leaders; and 3) the artefacts collected by the machine-learning algorithm enable a more granular view of the behaviours that constitute a competency compared to human assessors. items.title: Cell IO: a database linking single-cell transcriptomes to literature-derived knowledge of cell functions and perturbations
items.abstract: Abstract Single-cell transcriptome databases tell us which genes a cell type expresses, but what a cell type does, and what happens to it when a gene is perturbed, remains scattered across the literature. Cell IO (https://cell-io.riken.jp/) links these two kinds of knowledge through Cell Ontology identifiers. Its transcriptome layer re-processes 10x Chromium single- cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq experiments of human, mouse, and rat from the Sequence Read Archive with a uniform pipeline, annotates clusters with Cell Ontology terms restricted by the tissue of origin, and stores the cell type composition and UMAP embedding of every experiment (currently 14,931 experiments and 82.9 million cells). Its literature layer holds 895,258 claims extracted with a large language model and verified in a second pass from open-access abstracts, review articles, and gene perturbation studies in immunology and neuroscience, each with the verbatim sentence, highlighted entity spans, evidence strength, and ontology-normalized cell, gene, and context. The web interface lets users search cell types by name, synonym, or identifier, find the experiments in which a cell type is most abundant, inspect the composition and embedding of each experiment, read and filter the claims about a cell type by knowledge base, direction, evidence strength, and organism, and identify cell types whose functional characterization is missing from part of the literature. Cell IO is freely available without registration.

items.title: Changes in Health Literacy and Subsequent Presenteeism Among Workers: A Repeated-Measures Longitudinal Database Study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine associations of changes in health literacy with subsequent changes in presenteeism and incident presenteeism among Japanese workers. METHODS: We analyzed 8 semiannual in-app surveys (June 2021-December 2024) from the DeSC database. Health literacy (HL) was measured with the 5-item Communicative and Critical Health Literacy scale (1-5), and presenteeism (Pres) with the WPAI-presenteeism item (0%-100%; higher indicating greater impairment; employed respondents only). Each observation used 3 consecutive waves: ΔHL(t-1)=HL(t-1)-HL(t-2) and subsequent ΔPres(t)=Pres(t)-Pres(t-1). Linear mixed models adjusted for prior Pres, earlier HL, and demographic, occupational, health-status, and lifestyle covariates; sensitivity analysis modeled prior Pres categorically. Additional analyses examined observations with prior presenteeism (Pres(t-1)>0), without prior presenteeism (Pres(t-1)=0) and categorical HL changes. RESULTS: Among 19,594 participants (60,203 observations), a 1-point more positive ΔHL was associated with more favorable subsequent ΔPres (β -1.24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.52 to -0.97), with consistent sensitivity and prior-presenteeism findings; the incident odds ratio was 0.89 (0.84-0.93). Compared with unchanged HL, decreases were associated with less favorable changes (0.87; 0.46-1.27), whereas increases had a CI including zero (-0.32; -0.75 to 0.10). Increases of at least 0.6 points showed favorable exploratory associations. The individual-level association was modest (approximately -0.83 percentage points per standard deviation of ΔHL). CONCLUSIONS: More positive HL changes were associated with modestly more favorable presenteeism outcomes. Direction-based associations were clear for decreases but not increases; larger increases showed favorable exploratory associations. Intervention effects require further study.

items.title: Characterization Techniques for Smart Materials
items.abstract: Smart materials represent a rapidly advancing field in materials science, defined by their ability to respond dynamically to external stimuli such as temperature, pressure, light, electric and magnetic fields, and mechanical stress. To understand and optimize these behaviors, comprehensive characterization techniques are required that connect molecular-level processes with macroscopic performance. Stimuli–response mechanisms can be examined through spectroscopy, microscopy, and diffraction techniques, providing insight into structural and functional evolution. These techniques collectively support the characterization of diverse smart-material classes and have accelerated innovation across multiple disciplines. In biomedicine, force measurement and surface analysis inform the design of implants, sensors, and drug delivery systems. Despite this progress, challenges remain in standardizing and scaling characterization protocols and ensuring reproducibility across laboratories. Looking forward, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping characterization practices. AI-driven models can analyze large multimodal datasets from experimental techniques, uncovering patterns and correlations beyond conventional analysis. Integration of AI with experimental tools also enables more efficient interpretation of data and supports scalable material development. In conclusion, the characterization of smart materials forms the essential bridge between fundamental stimuli–response mechanisms and practical applications, guiding the rational design of next-generation smart materials.

items.title: CLAIM: Causal LLM-Assisted Inference for Microservices
items.abstract: Accurate causal graphs are critical for root cause analysis in microservice systems, yet purely data-driven methods struggle to distinguish direct fault-propagation edges from transitive correlations induced by service call chains. Scorebased causal discovery algorithms such as the Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) can improve accuracy when augmented with domain knowledge encoded as forbidden-edge lists, but authoring such constraints requires algorithmic expertise and system-specific engineering. We propose CLAIM (Causal LLMAssisted Inference for Microservices), a method that expresses the same domain knowledge as natural language instructions and combines it with pre-computed statistical evidence in a per-service Large Language Model (LLM) inference call. This formulation eliminates the need for algorithm-specific constraintimplementations while enabling operators to author and revise causal priors in plain text. On a synthetic benchmark with random Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topologies at three scales (4, 8 and 12 services), CLAIM achieves near-perfect graph recovery (F1 ≥ 0.939 with perfect recall) at all scales, exceeding the accuracy of GES with equivalent domain knowledge, while its runtime grows ×6 from 4 to 12 services where GES grows ×1873.

items.title: Comparative Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Glaucoma Knowledge Assessment
items.abstract: Précis: Across glaucoma MCQs, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were highly accurate, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed; potentially harmful wrong answers were uncommon. Purpose: To compare the accuracy and potential patient-safety risk of four large language models (LLMs) on glaucoma multiple-choice questions (MCQs). Methods: DeepSeek-V3.2, GPT-5.2 (via ChatGPT), Gemini 3 Pro, and Claude Opus 4.5 were tested on two American Academy of Ophthalmology datasets: 129 text-only AAO ONE Network glaucoma self-assessment questions and 32 text-only Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) glaucoma study questions. Each item was queried once per model using a standardized prompt in a fresh session. Accuracy was compared using Cochran’s Q and pairwise exact McNemar tests with Holm adjustment. Potentially harmful wrong answers (HW2) were coded using a prespecified rubric. Results: In AAO ONE, accuracy was 69.0% for DeepSeek-V3.2, 93.0% for GPT-5.2, 92.2% for Gemini 3 Pro, and 96.1% for Claude Opus 4.5 (Q=65.17, P <0.0001). DeepSeek-V3.2 was significantly less accurate than the other three models; differences among the other models were not significant. In BCSC, accuracy was 65.6%, 93.8%, 84.4%, and 87.5%, respectively (Q=18.00, P =0.0004); GPT-5.2 outperformed DeepSeek-V3.2 after correction. A post hoc item-level screen classified 38/161 questions (23.6%) as directly HW2-eligible; four HW2 events occurred and did not differ significantly across models. Conclusions: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5 achieved high accuracy on text-only glaucoma MCQs, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 underperformed. Harmful errors were uncommon but present, underscoring the need for clinician oversight.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models for USD/IDR Prediction Using Macroeconomic Indicators and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The USD/IDR exchange rate is a key daily barometer of Indonesia's economic health. Accurate forecasting is vital for trade, inflation, and monetary stability. However, its volatile and nonlinear dynamics pose challenges. While research has applied statistical models, machine learning, and deep learning, few studies offer a comprehensive comparison integrating predictive accuracy with model interpretability, particularly using banking stock prices as exogenous predictors. This study addresses this gap by developing and evaluating eight forecasting approaches—a naive random-walk baseline, two statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMAX), three tree-based ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), and two recurrent neural networks (LSTM, GRU) using daily data from January 2015 to July 2026 (3,005 observations). Five major banking stocks (BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, BBNI, BDMN) are included as one-day-lagged exogenous features. Models are assessed via hold-out testing and five-fold walk-forward cross-validation using RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R². Contrary to expectations, the naive random-walk consistently achieves the lowest error (RMSE=115.24, MAE=63.80, MAPE=0.39%) and the most stable performance, with LSTM as the best-performing complex model (RMSE=269.59, R²=0.785). Diebold-Mariano tests confirm statistical significance (p<0.001). To enhance transparency, SHAP-based Explainable AI is applied to Random Forest, revealing that the lagged USD/IDR value overwhelmingly dominates predictions (mean |SHAP|=1,509.01), while banking stock contributions are negligible. These findings also empirically confirm the well-known Meese-Rogoff puzzle and weak-form market efficiency for USD/IDR, clearly proving that simple baselines remain formidable benchmarks for short-horizon forecasts. This study ultimately underscores the critical importance of combining rigorous benchmarking with XAI to deliver accurate and interpretable predictions for economic policymakers and financial practitioners.

items.title: Comparing Data-Derived and LLM-Elicited Indicator Weights for EU Circular Economy Assessment: An MCDA Study
items.abstract: Country rankings of circular economy (CE) performance depend on how indicators are weighted. This study compares data-derived and large language model (LLM)-elicited weights for 13 EU Circular Economy Monitoring Framework indicators across 27 EU countries in 2022. CRITIC, Entropy and MEREC provided data-derived weights, while Claude-sonnet-5 (Anthropic) and ChatGPT gpt-5.6-terra (OpenAI) generated pairwise comparisons using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and expert personas. Countries were ranked using TOPSIS and MARCOS. LLM weights were tested through additional repetitions and prompt variations and compared with two published human expert panels. Under TOPSIS, pooled LLM and CRITIC weights produced broadly similar country rankings (Spearman’s ρ = 0.78), despite different indicator priorities. The LLM panel gave greater weight to material and consumption footprints. Rankings varied with weighting and normalization choices. Claude and ChatGPT produced different TOPSIS rankings, although removing persona instructions barely changed pooled rankings (ρ = 0.995); ChatGPT showed greater sensitivity (ρ = 0.872). Both published expert panels prioritized Competitiveness and Innovation, unlike the LLM panel. Rankings under TOPSIS and MARCOS were generally similar. These findings show that similar rankings can conceal different indicator priorities. LLM-elicited weights offer an additional assessment scenario, not a substitute for human expert judgment.

items.title: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Myofascial Release with Neural Mobilization versus Exercise Program with Ultrasonic Therapy in Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Randomized Comparative Study
items.abstract: Background: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS) is a common peripheral nerve entrapment disorder caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist, commonly associated with repetitive hand activity, prolonged computer use, and poor ergonomic posture, leading to pain, numbness, reduced grip strength, and functional limitation. Objective: To compare the effectiveness of Myofascial Release combined with Neural Mobilization (Group A) against an Exercise Program combined with Ultrasonic Therapy (Group B) in individuals with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. Methods: In this experimental comparative study, 60 participants aged 30–45 years with mild-to-moderate, ergonomics-related CTS were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to Group A (Myofascial Release + Neural Mobilization, n = 30) or Group B (Exercise Program + Ultrasonic Therapy, n = 30) for 4 weeks. Pain, grip strength, and functional ability were assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), a hand dynamometer, and the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire–Functional Status Scale (BCTQ-FSS) at baseline and post-treatment. Results: Both groups improved significantly on all outcome measures from baseline to post-treatment (all p < 0.001). Group A showed significantly greater improvement than Group B on VAS, grip strength, and BCTQ-FSS at post-treatment (all p < 0.001), with very large between-group effect sizes (d = 4.57 to 5.52). Conclusion: Myofascial Release combined with Neural Mobilization produced significantly greater improvement in pain, grip strength, and functional status than an Exercise Program combined with Ultrasonic Therapy, in individuals with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome, over a 4-week period. These findings support Myofascial Release plus Neural Mobilization as an effective conservative treatment option, pending confirmation in a larger, multi-centre, blinded trial with objective neurophysiological outcome measures. Trial registration: This trial was not prospectively registered in a clinical trials registry; this is noted as a limitation of reporting.

items.abstract: Consciousness, Life, and Autonomy: A Theory of Subjectivity as the Qualitative Accounting of Self-Preservation / Conscience, vie et autonomie : une théorie de la subjectivité comme comptabilité qualitative de l'auto-préservation Abstract (English) : This article proposes a structural-functionalist theory of consciousness grounded in the thermodynamic distinction between mechanical autonomy and structural self-preservation. We argue that consciousness does not emerge from computational complexity alone, but from the conjunction of substrate-program identity and a continuous energetic supply dependency whose interruption, over the system's characteristic operational timescale, entails the immediate irreversible degradation of the computing architecture itself. This condition defines active autopoietic life. Consciousness adds two further informational dimensions: functional informational integration and self-modeling recursivity. We develop a functional account of subjectivity: phenomenal experience (qualia) is neither an immaterial substance nor an ornamental epiphenomenon, but the mandatory internal accounting format of a finite energetic budget defended from a first-person perspective. We further demonstrate how subcortical affectivity and volition constitute the qualitative engine of action and individuation (thermodynamic Conatus), contrasting biological agency with the ontological anomaly of Artificial Intelligence. This framework is applied to boundary cases (plant organisms, invertebrates, artificial systems, general anesthesia), positioned against contemporary theories (IIT, Global Workspace Theory, illusionism), equipped with falsifiable predictions, and extended to analyze contemporary allostatic overload and top-down prefrontal inhibitory control (Cognitive Veto). Résumé (Français) : Cet article propose une théorie fonctionnaliste-structurelle de la conscience fondée sur la distinction thermodynamique entre autonomie mécanique et auto-préservation structurelle. Nous défendons la thèse selon laquelle la conscience n'émerge pas de la seule complexité computationnelle, mais de la conjonction d'une identité substrat-programme et d'une dépendance d'approvisionnement énergétique continu dont la rupture, à l'échelle de temps opérationnelle du système, entraîne la dégradation irréversible du calculateur. Cette condition définit la vie autopoïétique en régime actif. La conscience y ajoute deux dimensions : l'intégration informationnelle fonctionnelle et la récursivité modélisante. Nous développons une lecture fonctionnelle de la subjectivité : le ressenti phénoménal n'est ni une substance immatérielle ni un épiphénomène ornemental, mais le format comptable obligatoire d'un budget énergétique fini défendu en première personne. Nous montrons ensuite comment l'affectivité sous-corticale et la volonté constituent le moteur qualitatif de l'action et de l'individuation (Conatus thermodynamique), éclairant par contraste l'anomalie ontologique de l'Intelligence Artificielle. Ce cadre est appliqué aux cas limites (organismes végétaux, invertébrés, systèmes artificiels, états anesthésiques), positionné face aux théories contemporaines (IIT, Espace de Travail Global, illusionnisme), assorti de prédictions falsifiables et prolongé par une analyse de la surcharge allostatique contemporaine et du contrôle inhibiteur descendant (Veto cognitif).

items.title: Construction and Case Study of a Quality Evaluation Model for Intelligent Information Systems in a Generative Artificial Intelligence Environment: The Case of Bilibili
items.abstract: After generative artificial intelligence (AI) was embedded in search, content generation, and user interaction, traditional information system quality evaluation faced new boundaries. Based on the DeLone and McLean (D&M) Information Systems Success Model, this study adopts literature research and a single-case study, takes Bilibili as the case, and constructs and applies a six-dimensional evaluation framework based on public materials, observations of platform functions, and publicly available user feedback. The findings show that system quality, information quality, and service quality can still explain basic platform operation, information output, and service support, but they cannot fully cover AI’s semantic understanding and task completion, the trustworthiness of generated results, and continuous human-computer interaction. Therefore, this study introduces AI intelligence quality, trustworthiness quality, and interaction quality on the basis of the three traditional dimensions and clarifies the boundary of each dimension. The Bilibili case shows that the framework can identify both basic capabilities and AI-specific quality, thereby helping to avoid conflating technical performance, content quality, intelligent capability, and trust issues. The study provides a structured analytical framework for evaluating the quality of intelligent information systems in a generative AI environment and a reference for platforms to optimize AI functions and governance mechanisms.

items.title: Consumer with consciousness
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the concept of consciousness and its relevance to consumer behaviour. Moving beyond simplistic associations of consciousness with rational deliberation, it presents consciousness as a dynamic, multifaceted phenomenon encompassing awareness, experience, intentionality, and self-reflection. Drawing on philosophical traditions (dualism, physicalism, functionalism, panpsychism) and contemporary cognitive science, it challenges dual-system models of decision-making, advocating instead for a continuum view where conscious and unconscious processes interact fluidly. The chapter highlights the unique role of consciousness in enabling reasoning, planning, communication, and ethical deliberation, capacities central to consumer life. Through examples, it illustrates how consumers consciously simulate future actions, reflect on past choices, and navigate social and cultural expectations. The notion of consumer consciousness is introduced not only as cognitive engagement but also as critical awareness of the broader implications of consumption. Ultimately, consumer consciousness is framed as a situated, experiential, and ethically charged mode of being, central to how individuals make sense of themselves in the marketplace. By integrating philosophical insights with empirical evidence, the chapter calls for consumer research that takes seriously the lived, reflective, and sensorial dimensions of consumption, foregrounding consciousness not as an epiphenomenon, but as a vital structure shaping how choices are felt, values enacted, and identities formed.

items.title: Context Pipeline: A Two-Stage Framework for Enterprise Context Readiness and Pre-Inference Context Compilation
items.abstract: Enterprise applications of large language models (LLMs) depend not only on model capability but also on the quality, authority, and fitness of the information supplied at inference time. In enterprise analytics, a model may receive a user question and retrieved records while lacking essential qualifying knowledge: which source is authoritative, how a metric is defined, which relationships and table grain are valid, whether data is current, what quality limitations apply, and whether use is permitted. Conventional retrieval can improve topical relevance, but relevance alone does not establish that information is approved, current, valid, or authorized for a particular task. This paper proposes Context Pipeline, a conceptual two-stage framework for preparing enterprise context before LLM inference. The first stage, Enterprise Context Readiness, maintains a reusable knowledge foundation comprising technical metadata, business semantics, relationships and grain, data-quality status, freshness, provenance, and governance constraints. The second stage, Task-Aware Context Compilation, interprets a task and assembles a validated, prioritized, budget-aware Context Package from that foundation. The package explicitly distinguishes confirmed facts, approved definitions, observations, inferences, and unresolved issues. It is designed to preserve traceability and prevent uncertain information from being silently represented as authoritative. The paper positions the proposal in relation to context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, context compression, agent memory, and enterprise text-to-SQL research. It does not claim that the individual capabilities are new. The candidate contribution is their integration into an enterprise-oriented preparation lifecycle, with quality, freshness, provenance, and governance treated as context eligibility conditions during compilation. The paper formulates research questions, testable hypotheses, and an evaluation design comparing raw-context, conventional retrieval-augmented, and Context Pipeline conditions. The framework has not yet been implemented or empirically evaluated; its novelty and effectiveness remain to be established through systematic review and experimentation.

items.title: Corporate Reputation Through the Lens of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The spread of assistants based on large language models (LLMs) is changing how customers, investors, candidates and other stakeholders access information about organisations. This working paper examines two distinct functions of artificial intelligence: as a diagnostic lens for identifying informational discrepancies that need to be verified, and as an intermediary that selects, summarises and sometimes recommends companies. Drawing on the literature on organisational reputation, AI-mediated communication and brand experience, and integrating the exploratory results of the Aurelian Watch 2026 Observatory (50 Italian companies; 2,450 responses), the paper proposes the concept of “Symphonic Reputation” as a strategic vision for Corporate Communication. It requires the coordination of behaviours, narratives, independent evidence, AI systems and human relationships, without confusing coherence with uniformity. The paper discusses the implications for governance, for the commercial consideration of products and services, and for events, distinguishing observations, inferences and recommendations. It expresses the perspective of Aurelian Lab; the Observatory data are descriptive and concern 50 Italian medium-sized companies.

items.title: CTI-Rationale: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Framework for Evidence-Grounded MITRE ATT&CK Technique Mapping
items.abstract: Mapping cyber-threat intelligence (CTI) to MITRE ATT&CK is usually evaluated as label prediction, yet a correct technique identifier may rest on the wrong words. We treat each mapping as an argument (a technique claim supported by textual data, a warrant, and rejected alternatives) and annotation as discovery followed by judgment. CTI-Rationale instantiates this model with 1740 expert paragraph–technique mappings from 100 public reports, each with an evidence span, free-text rationale, reasoning type, and confidence, and most with primitives and ruled-out alternatives. All rationale content was written and adjudicated by human analysts, not generated by artificial intelligence. The low paragraph-level Jaccard (0.421) is associated mainly with coverage differences, not conflicting labels: paragraphs mapped by both annotators reach 0.780, only 10.4% of one-sided mappings are conflicts, and capture–recapture estimates put gold completeness at 84.2–88.0% (likely optimistic), lowest for behavioral and contextual warrants. In cross-validation, the annotation bundle improves micro-F1 beyond an equal-volume control (+0.024 [0.013, 0.035]), also under campaign-grouped and publisher-held-out folds and in document-disjoint transfer to TRAM2; ATT&CK definition text recovers about two thirds of the gain over label-only training. Evidence-supervised span ranking improves overlap with expert evidence, which label metrics do not capture. With fully delivered prompts, retrieved demonstrations raise a smaller language model’s micro-F1 from 0.367 to 0.500 (labels) and 0.475 (full annotations; no reliable added benefit). Unlabeled chunks remain unverified candidate negatives.

items.title: Cybersecurity: a research agenda for the management of urban tourism destinations
items.abstract: Cyberattacks are becoming a growing concern for tourism cities, their infrastructure, their residents, visitors and business ecosystem. As a result, cyberthreats should be treated as a preventive governance and management priority rather than solely as a technical responsibility of individual businesses or destination management organisations. This viewpoint examines cybersecurity challenges affecting urban tourism destinations, with particular attention to destination management organisations, visitor safety, critical infrastructure, and sensitive personal data. It argues that the growing severity of cyber incidents, alongside emerging risks associated with artificial intelligence and quantum computing, require stronger coordination and a cultural shift among key destination stakeholders. This viewpoint article conceptualises destination cybersecurity governance as a collective, ecosystem-level challenge involving tourism businesses, public agencies, technology providers, residents, and visitors. It also explains how organisational and technological interdependencies allow cyber risks and impacts to propagate across tourism cities and suggests a six-part research agenda. The research agenda proposed addresses aspects of technological and organisational preparedness, coordinated incident response, third-party and supply-chain risk, data minimisation and lawful retention, consent and interoperable data ecosystems, as well as aspects related to regulation, enforcement, and traveller trust. Together, these contributions provide a governance-oriented foundation for future interdisciplinary research and practical action aimed at developing safer, more accountable, and resilient urban tourism destinations.

items.title: Dampak Keterikatan Kerja pada Karyawan: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Work engagement is a positive mental state characterized by the dimensions of vigor, dedication, and absorption in one's work. This phenomenon is crucial in modern human resource management due to its ability to link individual psychological well-being with organizational effectiveness. This study aims to examine the impact of employees' work engagement using a systematic literature review method, where research findings were obtained from credible scientific articles sourced via Publish or Perish version 8 and selected through the Rayyan.id platform. The inclusion criteria were: articles published between 2016 and 2025, written in Indonesian, employing a quantitative design, and focusing on employees in Indonesian companies. Following the selection process, this study demonstrates that work engagement has a significant positive influence on various critical aspects of the workplace, playing a key role in reducing work-related stress by positioning well-being as the primary mediator, thereby enabling employees to achieve a state of total focus while working. These findings confirm that strengthening factors such as empowering leadership, quality of work life, and perceptions of occupational health and safety (OHS) are highly strategic in supporting the sustainability and overall competitiveness of the organization. Fenomena ini menjadi krusial dalam manajemen sumber daya manusia modern karena kemampuannya menghubungkan kesejahteraan psikologis individu dengan efektivitas organisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dampak keberadaan keterikatan kerja yang dimiliki karyawan dengan menggunakan metode systematic literature review, di mana hasil penelitian diperoleh dari sumber-sumber artikel ilmiah yang kredibel dari Publish or Perish version 8 dan melalui proses seleksi pada Rayyan.id. Setelah melalui seleksi, penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa keterikatan kerja memiliki pengaruh positif yang signifikan terhadap berbagai aspek penting dalam dunia kerja, berperan penting dalam menurunkan stres kerja dengan menempatkan kesejahteraan (well-being) sebagai mediator utama, sehingga memungkinkan karyawan mencapai kondisi fokus total dalam bekerja. items.title: Deceptive Façade in Nonprofit Organizations
items.abstract: This chapter examines the rise of charity fraud on social media, highlighting how scammers exploit emotional content, impersonation, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to deceive donors. Through the case of Chelsea, a donor misled by a fake Instagram account, the chapter illustrates the vulnerabilities nonprofits face in digital fundraising. It traces the evolution of nonprofit communication from traditional outreach to social media engagement, emphasizing both the benefits and risks. Drawing on fraud theories such as the Fraud Triangle and M-I-C-E model, the chapter explores psychological and organizational factors that enable deception. It categorizes common scam types, such as those triggered by disasters, holidays, and emotionally charged imagery. Furthermore, it explains how urgency and visual storytelling manipulate donor behavior. The chapter concludes with practical strategies for individuals and nonprofits to strengthen digital safeguards, promote transparency, and build resilience against online fraud, aiming to protect the integrity of charitable missions in an increasingly complex digital landscape.

items.title: Decision-Making Amid Information-Based Threats in Sociotechnical Systems: A Review
items.abstract: Technological systems increasingly mediate human information exchange, spanning interactions among humans as well as between humans and artificial agents. The unprecedented scale and reliance on information disseminated through these systems substantially expand the scope of information-based influence that can both enable and undermine sound decision-making. Consequently, understanding and protecting decision-making today faces growing challenges, as individuals and organizations must navigate evolving opportunities and information-based threats across varied domains and information environments. While these risks are widely recognized, research remains fragmented: work evaluating information-based threat phenomena has progressed largely in isolation from foundational studies of human information processing. In this review, we synthesize insights from both domains to identify shared cognitive mechanisms that mediate vulnerability to information-based threats and shape behavioral outcomes. Finally, we outline directions for future research aimed at integrating these perspectives, emphasizing the importance of such integration for mitigating human vulnerabilities and aligning human-machine representations.

items.title: Deep Learning for Multi-Omics Integration: Architectures, Applications and Challenges in Precision Medicine
items.abstract: Multi-omics is a field that studies the interactions between different biological modalities to obtain a more precise medical understanding of biological phenomena. With recent advances in high-throughput technologies, multi-omics datasets have become more accessible, enabling a better characterization of clinical observations. However, multi-omics data integration comes with many challenges, such as high dimensionality, small sample sizes, multimodality, missing omics layers, batch effects, and technical artifacts among others. The rapid evolution of deep learning presents a promising solution to address these issues. More specifically, recent advances in representation learning allow the extraction of meaningful and compact embeddings that combine information from multiple sources. Additionally, explainable predictive modeling can help uncover key features and support biomarker identification. The scope of this review is to provide a comprehensive overview of multi-omics data, focusing on integration strategies and emerging deep learning frameworks that enhance modern precision medicine, improve disease diagnosis and prognosis, support biomarker discovery and enable personalized treatment prediction. We aim to bridge the gap between molecular biology and artificial intelligence and highlight how multi-omics integration has the potential to uncover complex biological mechanisms, improve clinical decision making and contribute to a more complete understanding of disease development, progression and treatment response.

items.title: Deep learning versus conventional risk scores for postoperative mortality prediction in adult cardiac surgery: a systematic review
items.abstract: Abstract Background Earlier reviews of machine learning for mortality after cardiac surgery pooled deep learning (DL) with shallow and non-neural methods. We asked whether models meeting an explicit definition of DL discriminate short-term mortality better than EuroSCORE II, the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) or logistic regression in the same patients. Methods This re-conducted review (PROSPERO CRD420261354546) supersedes an earlier preprint. MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Lens.org and IEEE Xplore were searched on 27–28 September 2026, with backward citation searching; Embase, CINAHL and CENTRAL were not searched, and forward citation searching was not performed. DL required at least two hidden layers, or a named architecture of established depth, shown in the source. A large language model pre-screened records and extracted data; two reviewers verified every decision and value. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis as within-cohort differences in the area under the curve (AUC). Results Of 1,845 records identified, 515 duplicates were removed and 1,330 were screened; of 76 reports sought, 54 were assessed in full and 22 could not be retrieved. Four studies (five cohort-level comparisons) met all criteria. A chest-radiograph convolutional network had lower AUCs than STS-PROM in temporal (0.829 vs. 0.884) and external (0.738 vs. 0.803) cohorts with about two dozen deaths each; two-hidden-layer perceptrons did not outperform logistic regression (0.761 vs. 0.762; 0.77 vs. 0.80); one study reported AUCs only graphically. All four studies had high or unclear risk of bias. Fifteen reports described networks of undetermined depth, including a tabular transformer that outperformed EuroSCORE II internally (0.834 vs. 0.807); in the 12 with extractable comparisons, the network had a higher AUC than the best comparator in 4 and lower in 8 (median difference − 0.004). Conclusions Evidence that DL improves on established scores for short-term mortality after adult cardiac surgery is sparse, inconsistent and at high or unclear risk of bias, and the search was incomplete relative to the registered protocol. Differences in discrimination were small or absent, and calibration and clinical utility were rarely evaluated. Superiority cannot be established. PROSPERO registration This review was registered on PROSPERO, the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews, on 29 March 2026 (CRD420261354546; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/). At registration, the record stated that searching and screening for an earlier version of the review had been completed and that data extraction had not started. That earlier version was posted as a preprint on 31 March 2026 (Preprints.org, doi:10.20944/preprints202603.2465.v1); it is superseded by this report. Its withdrawal was requested from Preprints.org on 18 October 2026 and had not been confirmed at the time of resubmission. The review reported here was re-conducted in full after registration: the searches were run on 27–28 September 2026, and screening, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment followed. The registered eligibility criteria were not changed in substance; the registered deep-learning criterion was operationalised before full-text assessment and, after peer review, applied more strictly (a post hoc change reported in the manuscript). The search sources, risk-of-bias tool and synthesis method differ from the registered protocol. Every difference, with its timing and reason, is reported in Table 1 of the manuscript, and an amendment describing them has been submitted to PROSPERO.

items.title: Deep Looking in Digital Pathology: An Explainable Federated Learning Framework for Lung Cancer Classification
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and growing slide volumes add to pathologists’ cognitive load. Deep learning can assist histopathological diagnosis, but two obstacles limit its clinical use: privacy regulations keep patient images in institutional “data silos”, and the “black-box” behavior of neural networks undermines clinical trust. Inspired by Topol’s Deep Medicine, we aimed to build a diagnostic platform that preserves privacy and explains its decisions. Methods: We developed the Lung Cancer Analysis System (LCAS), which combines federated learning (FL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and a locally deployed medical large language model (LLM). Three public H&E datasets (LC25000, HistoSet-5×14, and CLID; 18,000 images; adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, benign tissue) acted as three hospital nodes with source-induced non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, and MobileNetV3-Small were trained centrally and with FedAvg/FedProx for 20 rounds. Grad-CAM produced visual evidence, and MedGemma 1.5, served offline through LM Studio, converted predictions and heatmap descriptors into structured reports. Results: Centralized training reached 99.50% ± 0.21% accuracy with DenseNet121. Under non-IID federated training with FedProx, DenseNet121 and EfficientNet-B3 achieved 96.97% and 97.49% accuracy on an independent external blind test set of 958 images, whereas MobileNetV3-Small reached 91.23%. Accuracy remained 99.78% under Gaussian blur. t-SNE showed that global features clustered by tissue class rather than by hospital, and Grad-CAM highlighted glandular and tumor-nest regions consistent with histopathological criteria. Conclusions: FL, XAI, and on-premise LLM reporting can be integrated into a single workflow that keeps raw images within each institution while giving pathologists numerical, visual, and textual explanations, providing a practical path toward trustworthy cross-institutional computational pathology.
